_doc: THE LANGUAGE OF THE PIECE (decibel PLAN 2.3; RUNNING_LOG §307; DEC-90: 'the piece uses a variation of anthony braxton's language musics, we will use the badges from p1&2, that format and then come up with a symbal for each and a color'). `badge`: the format, read from piece #1's flocking badge (string_quartet_no1-composer/docs/notation_instructions/images/flocking_badge.svg). `types`: HIS six, in his order — each the piece's own sound type, the Braxton Language Type it varies (his handout's number, name and sign, described in words; the handout itself is at the Library of Congress), and where it is in the piece. A type's `symbol` and `colour` are EMPTY until he chooses. `candidates.<type>`: signs put to him — each an icon drawn in a 36 × 36 box (`svg`, in currentColor), where it comes from, what speaks for it. tools/language/build_page.js draws them as badges on score/public/language/index.html.

badge.from: piece #1 (the flocking badge): a 36 px rounded square of dark slate, the sign in it in light blue. Piece #2's badge (the three orbits) is black discs and lines on white, no square.

types.name: short attacks

braxton.name: SHORT ATTACKS
braxton.sign: three small open triangles, apart — two pointing left, one up

types.inThePiece: the opening's impulses · the three body problem

types.name: trills

braxton.name: TRILLS
braxton.sign: a line of tall, deep waves

types.inThePiece: section 2 — thirty trills, each into a petal hit

braxton.name: ACCENTED LONG SOUND
braxton.sign: a narrow closed wedge that runs on as a line — the accent, then the long sound

types.name: multiphonics

braxton.name: MULTIPHONICS
braxton.sign: three small five-sided shapes, like little houses, one upright and two upside down

types.inThePiece: the drones — each player's multiphonic, recorded and stretched

types.name: ‹a name wanted›
types.inThePiece: the beating section — a held note against a sine

types.name: scattered strikes
types.inThePiece: section 5 — the ensemble's strikes, the electronics answering

braxtonTwelve: 2 Accented long sound — a narrow wedge that runs on as a line
3 Trills — a line of tall waves
4 Staccato line formings — a dashed line
5 Intervallic formings — a line that jumps up and down in square steps
7 Short attacks — three small open triangles
8 Angular attacks — a chain of sharp Z shapes
9 Legato formings — a long smooth wave
10 Diatonic formings — a smooth wave with small strokes across it
11 Gradient formings — a smooth wave with arrowheads along it
12 Sub-identity formings — a small square, then a line

shortAttacks.name: Braxton's own
shortAttacks.from: Language Type 7, his handout: three small open triangles, two pointing left and one up
shortAttacks.for: It IS the sign of the language the piece varies. A player who knows Braxton reads it at once.

shortAttacks.name: marcato
shortAttacks.from: the standard sign for a marked, forceful attack — an open wedge over the note
shortAttacks.for: His candidate. Every player knows it. One clean shape, readable at 36 px.
shortAttacks.svg: <polyline points='9.5,26 18,9.5 26.5,26' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='3.2' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='miter'/>

shortAttacks.name: marcato, scattered
shortAttacks.from: the marcato wedge, three times, at uneven heights
shortAttacks.for: Says SEVERAL attacks, irregular — closer to what the type is than one accent; keeps the known sign.
shortAttacks.svg: <g fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2.3' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='miter'><polyline points='4,22 8.5,12.5 13,22'/><polyline points='13.5,28 18,18.5 22.5,28'/><polyline points='23,17.5 27.5,8 32,17.5'/></g>

shortAttacks.name: staccatissimo, scattered
shortAttacks.from: the standard sign for the shortest note — a small solid wedge — three times
shortAttacks.for: It means SHORT, where the marcato means MARKED. A solid triangle: Braxton's shape, filled.

shortAttacks.name: staccato dots, scattered
shortAttacks.for: The plainest. Risk: three dots read as an ellipsis, or as nothing, at this size.
